summary: Three Opus audits (isolation, config fidelity, test integrity) on the same day's eval-subject work found nine confirmed defects, seven of them introduced that day. Every fix below is falsified: reverted, the named test goes red.
details: ISOLATION: `sandbox_room_for` branched on `"/" in real_id` to detect a Discord `<guild>/<channel>` pair. A SIGNAL group id is base64 and carries slashes too, so every Signal snapshot case -- most of the converted corpus -- was minted a Discord-shaped NUMERIC id on the Signal platform, losing the `g-` marker that tells a reader, and any cleanup query, that a row belongs to an eval rather than a real room. Now branches on platform, with four tests (the function had none).

CONFIG: `divergences()` iterated only DEPLOYMENT-stated keys, on the stated reasoning that an example-stated key the deployment omits 'is a code default for both'. False. The audit measured 44 such keys: the subject takes the EXAMPLE's value, production takes `nora/config.py`'s default. They agree today by curation alone. That is the original 65-value divergence reached through the half of the key space the gate was not looking at. It now compares both directions, example-only keys against the code default.

The first cut of that fix had the same disease: `config_default` returned the field's ANNOTATION when there was no default, compared `'Nora'` against `<class 'str'>`, and reported 57 divergences that were not. It now returns None for anything unresolvable -- 'cannot check' is not 'agrees', which is the rule its own docstring already stated.

TEST INTEGRITY: seven tests could not fail, including the one added that morning specifically to close a falsification gap. Its fixture wrote an `identity.toml` BYTE-IDENTICAL to `_DEFAULT_IDENTITY`, so `"persons.miles_novak" in identity` held whether or not the roster wiring existed; its `persons` assertion used `persons = "*"`, the very value `policy_for` claims never to widen to; and `_ROOM_FIELDS`'s tail could be deleted with everything green because no fixture room carried those fields. The fixture now states three people and all nine room fields.

`test_a_skipped_prefix_is_not_taken_from_the_deployment` was fully vacuous -- the fixture stated no `obs.` key at all and `FORCE_OFF` wrote the booleans anyway, so removing `"obs."` from SKIP_PREFIX was a full pass. It now uses non-boolean keys only SKIP_PREFIX can exclude. `materialise()` had no test anywhere, while the test named for it called `divergences()`; it now has a refusal test plus a positive control.

`media.encryption_key_env` sat in SKIP_PREFIX with no stated reason. It is an env var NAME, not a credential, so skipping it protected nothing -- and it left the subject reading the example's variable, so media custody was OFF even on the deploy host with the real key exported. Removed; the gate immediately reported the divergence it had been hiding.

`NORA_DATA_HOST_ROOT` used `os.environ.setdefault`, which is unsound on exactly the host the comment claimed it was right for: `store.data_dir` is the case workdir, and letting compose's value win means the backend bind-mounts the DEPLOYMENT's data root into the sandbox container while the daemon writes into the workdir. Fail-open, plus an eval container mounting the deployment's data directory. Now set unconditionally.

The test suite was broken for everyone but its author: `config.evaluation.toml` is gitignored and written only by `python -m evals`, while every subject composes it -- 7 of 10 `test_subject_obtain` tests fail on a fresh clone, and an existing checkout silently composes whatever a previous run left. A session fixture now materialises it, preferring the deployment's own config and falling back to a stated one, which is the same generator on a stated input rather than a second composition path.
`config_default` moved to `nora/subject/` because the layered contract forbids `evals/` importing `nora.config` (`tests/test_boundaries.py`) -- caught by the gate, not by review.
